canonical_title: Candidate learning generation and human promotion decisions are structurally separate contracts; the builder proves promotion without holding promotion authority
summary: Stage 2B generated four candidate learning items as maturity CANDIDATE / authority_effect NONE / generated_by.actor_class synthesis, with the schema's own .strict() validation structurally rejecting any promotion-shaped field (reviewed_by, founder_approval, institutional_approval, status, promotion_scope, approving_authority). Stage 3A then materialized Mission Control's already-made promotion decision into separate PromotionReviewSchema records referencing that decision by decision_ref, explicitly stating the builder has no promotion authority and is only proving a decision that was made elsewhere. The two stages together demonstrate the candidate/promotion boundary holding in practice across a real generate-then-promote cycle, not merely as an untested schema constraint.

claims.text: None of the four Stage 2B candidates contained any prohibited promotion-shaped field, confirmed independently both by the schema's own .strict() validation (which would fail if any such field were present) and by a separate defensive grep across all four files that matched nothing -- the separation is enforced structurally, not only by convention.

evidence.locator: Line 118: 'No prohibited field (reviewed_by, founder_approval, founder_approved, institutional_approval, institutionalised_by, institutionalized_by, supersedes, superseded_by, risk_resolution, status, promotion_scope, approving_authority, or any other unrecognized key) appears in any candidate -- confirmed both by the schema's own .strict() rejection... and by an independent defensive grep across all four files, which matched nothing.'

claims.text: Stage 3A explicitly frames its own work as materializing and proving a promotion decision Mission Control had already made, not as a new independent judgment, and explicitly states the builder holds no promotion authority -- the promotion record references the controlling human decision by decision_ref rather than asserting the builder's own approval.

evidence.locator: Line 21: 'Materialize and prove Mission Control's already-made human review/promotion decision... This is proof of an already-made decision, not a new independent promotion judgment -- the builder has no promotion authority.'

claims.text: Across both stages, no candidate or promotion record in this mission ever used INSTITUTIONALISED maturity, ORGANIZATION_WIDE scope, or a claimed Founder approval -- promotion approving authority is recorded as mission-control throughout, matching the actual decision, and no supersession edge or registry-publication automation was created by the builder.

evidence.locator: Line 176: 'No INSTITUTIONALISED status or ORGANIZATION_WIDE scope was used. No Founder approval was claimed (approving authority is mission-control throughout, matching the actual decision)... these are static, human-decision-materializing data files, written and committed by the authorized builder, not by an autonomous writer.'

conditions: Applies to any AI-generated content whose downstream consequence (here, organizational authority/institutional weight) must remain strictly separated from the act of generating it.

Requires both a structural enforcement mechanism (a strict schema that rejects authority-shaped fields on the generation side) and a procedural one (an explicit decision_ref back to the actual human/governance decision on the promotion side) -- this mission proved both together, not just one.
anti_patterns: Allowing a single contract or schema to represent both an AI-generated draft and its eventual approved/institutional state, which makes it structurally possible for generation to silently imply authority it never earned.

Having the same actor generate a candidate and then also record its own promotion, even if the fields are technically separate -- this mission kept the promotion step tied to a separate, named, already-made Mission Control decision (decision_ref) rather than the builder's own judgment at promotion time.
